title: Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal denied; the SJC answered “No” to whether any specification of error should be sustained, rejecting all seventeen specifications in six categories. MAP's verdict of guilty on three charges and censure of indefinite suspension until satisfactory evidence of repentance were upheld. The SJC assessed transcription costs equally, while encouraging MAP to consider absorbing the entire cost. Vote: one dissent (Meyerhoff); Burnett and Cannata absent; White recused.
first_summary: The SJC denied TE John Hardie's appeal from his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges and indefinite suspension. Applying clear-error review, it rejected his procedural, evidentiary, scheduling, prejudice, and censure claims and upheld the lower court. Transcription costs were split equally, with encouragement that MAP absorb them.
summary: TE John Hardie appealed his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges of breaking ordination vows and indefinite suspension, alleging seventeen procedural and evidentiary errors. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, the SJC denied every specification and upheld the judgment and censure. It found no clear error in the BCO 31-2 investigation, indictment/prosecutor process, commission membership, evidence rulings, scheduling, alleged prejudice, or censure. It assessed transcription costs equally while encouraging MAP to absorb them, and cautioned that an absent commissioner's vote might support a future challenge.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2015-08, TE John Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery, SJC Decision on Appeal March 3, 2016; Panel's proposed decision drafted by RE Jones and RE Nusbaum, edited by Panel and amended/approved by SJC on roll call (lines 1–3, 11–19, 419–421).
evidence_notes.dispute: Hardie appealed MAP's judgment finding him guilty of three charges of breaking ordination vows and imposing indefinite suspension until he gave satisfactory evidence of repentance; he alleged seventeen specifications of error in six categories—procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of reasonable indulgence, prejudice, hurrying to decision, and disproportionate censure (lines 17–19, 67–69, 88, 397–411).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC denied appeal and upheld MAP. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, it rejected each specification: BCO 31-2 investigation/commission formation; indictment/prosecutor process; RE Edwards bias/absence; parliamentarian advice; witnesses joining prosecution; evidentiary rulings; scheduling/indulgence; prejudice; and censure. It held indefinite suspension was the only appropriate censure under BCO 30-1 absent repentance/restitution (lines 79–88, 92–411).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC declined to decide whether a temporarily absent commission member's vote could invalidate the judgment, saying a challenge could arise but the record was insufficient (lines 200–209). It assumed the moderator signed the prosecutor's indictment but found no BCO violation (lines 158–164). Costs were split equally, with encouragement for MAP to absorb all (lines 413–417).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The opinion notes Category I.a issues are essentially the same as Complaint SJC 2015-03 and that the only ROC documents on them are materials from Case 2015-03 included by reference (lines 97–98); no separate result from 2015-03 is supplied or relied on for the disposition.
